Court No. - 74
Case :- Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. - 3726 of 2023
Applicant :- Vishnu Mishra

Opposite Party :- State of U.P.
Counsel for Applicant :- Saurabh Raj Srivastava,Reema Pandey,Sr. Advocate
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.,Abhishek Kumar Yadav
Hon'ble Sameer Jain,J.
1.
Rejoinder affidavit filed today on behalf of the applicant is taken on record.

2. Heard Sri G.S. Chaturvedi, learned Senior Advocate assisted by Sri Saurabh Raj Srivastava and Smt. Reema Pandey, learned counsels for the applicant, Sri Abhishek Kumar Yadav, learned counsel for the inormant and Sri Sanjay Kumar Yadav, learned AGA for the State.
3. The instant bail application has been filed seeking release of the applicant on bail in Case Crime No. 0273 of 2020, under Sections 323, 347, 387, 449, 506, 419, 420, 467, 468, 471, 474, 120B IPC and Section 66-C, 66-D Indian Information Technology Act, Police Station Gopiganj, District Sant Ravidas Nagar (Bhadohi) during pendency of the trial.
4. FIR of the present case was lodged on 04.08.2020 under Sections 323, 506, 449, 347, 387 IPC against applicant and his parents.

According to the FIR father of the applicant was Member of Legislative Assembly from Gyanpur constituency and in relation he is the brother of the informant and is forcibly residing in the house of informant by threatening him since the year 2001.

It is further mentioned in the FIR that father of the applicant namely Vijay Mishra, Ex. M.L.A. has taken control over the firm of the informant M/s Krishna Mohan Tiwari and started transferring the Vishnu Mishra vs State Of U.P. on 20 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/139477586/
1 amount either in the accounts of his own firms or in the accounts of the applicant and her mother i.e. co-accused Ram Lali Mishra.

sentences.text: It is further mentioned in the FIR that by threatening the informant, co-accused Vijay Mishra (father of the applicant) forcibly obtained signature of the informant on cheques and he has forcibly possessed entire banking documents of the informant and he is continuously harassing the informant and his entire family members.

According to the FIR,
Vijay Mishra, the father of the applicant is pressurizing the informant to execute a Will in favour of the applicant.

Submission on behalf of the applicant:
5. Learned counsel for the applicant submitted that entire allegation made against the applicant and his parents in the FIR as well as in the statements of the witnesses recorded during investigation are totally false and baseless and neither applicant nor his parents ever possessed the property of the informant and they never took control over the alleged firm of the informant and no fraud and cheating has ever been committed by either applicant or his parents.
6. Learned counsel for the applicant further submits that as per allegation made in the FIR and in the statements of the witnesses including the statement of the informant recorded during investigation applicant and his parents are continuously harassing the informant and his family members since the year 2001 but FIR of the present case was lodged in the month of August, 2020 i.e. after abut two decades and this fact itself shows that entire story narrated by the informant in the FIR is totally false and baseless and no cogent and plausible explanation has been given by the informant for such inordinate delay in lodging the FIR of the present case.

7. Learned counsel for the applicant further submits that the FIR of the present case is politically motivated and applicant belongs to well khown political family of U.P. and his father i.e. co-accused Vijay Mishra was Ex. M.L.A. and he four times consecutively remained M.L.A from Gyanpur constituency and co-accused Ram Lali Mishra, the mother of the applicant was also M.L.A. from Sonebhadra, District Mirzapur.

He further submits that applicant throughout his student life remained in boarding and informant was appointed his guardian while applicant was in Dehradoon between the year 1998-2006 and from the year 2006-2016 applicant was in United States of America and he returned from abroad in the year 2012 and from the year 2012-2016 he stayed in Delhi and was doing business in Delhi.
He further submits that the relationship of the family of the applicant and informant was cordial one.

8. He further submits, firm M/s Krishna Mohan Tiwari is a partnership firm, in which, along with informant, the mother of the applicant i.e. co-accused Smt. Ram Lali Mishra and one Ashok Shukla are also partners and on the basis of partnership deed dated 20.12.2006 a bank account in State Bank of India Gopiganj Branch was opened, which still exists.

sentences.text: He further submits that from the perusal of the partnership deed dated 20.12.2006, which has been annexed as Annexure-7 to the affidavit, it appears that there is arbitration clause in it with respect to any dispute if arose between the partners but informant only with intention to grab the entire business of the partnership firm lodged FIR of the present case pretending himself sole proprietor of the firm totally on the basis of false and frivolous allegation.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the applicant further submits that other partners of the firm co-accused Smt.
Ram Lali Mishra, the mother of the applicant and Ashok Shukla preferred a petition under Section 9 Arbitration and Conciliation Act against the informant before District Judge, Bhadohi.

The petition filed by them was partly allowed by the District Judge, Bhadohi on 22.02.2021 and in the order dated 22.02.2021 District Judge, Bhadohi admitted the partnership deed, bank account and other business documents of the firm.

He further submits that against the order dated 22.02.2021 passed by District Judge, Bhadohi, the mother of the applicant i.e. co-accused Ram Lali Mishra and Ashok Shukla being partners of the firm preferred an appeal before this Court.

He further submits that informant also preferred an appeal before this Court against the order dated 22.02.2021 passed by District Judge, Bhadohi and this Court on 05.08.2021 clubbed both the appeals filed by the informant and mother of the applicant and Ashok Shukla.

10. He further submits that both the partners of the firm M/s Krishna Mohan Tiwari also preferred a petition under Section 11 for appointment of the Arbitrator and on 16.09.2022 this Court has appointed Hon'ble Justice Vineet Saran, retired Judge of the Supreme Court as Arbitrator.
11. He further submits that from the above mentioned facts it is apparent that dispute with regard to partnership firm is pending between informant and family of the applicant.

12. Learned counsel for the applicant further submits that allegation that father of the applicant has taken over possession of the entire property and business of the informant is pertinently false and baseless and in fact informant is continuously disposing the property of the partnership firm and he also withdrew about rupees 6 Crores from the current account of the firm.

13. He further submits that informant also issued five cheques in favour of the companies, which belong to the family of the applicant and four cheques issued by the informant have been dishonoured and in this regard proceedings under Section 138 N.I. Act are pending against him and out of above mentioned four cheques, three cheques were issued in the month of July, 2020 while one cheque was issued by the informant in November, 2020

, therefore, this fact clearly suggests that by lodging false FIR of the present case on 04.08.2020 against applicant and his parents informant wanted to escape from his liability to pay the cheques amount.
14. He further submits that from the perusal of the FIR it appears that there is no allegation against the applicant and entire allegation is against his father Vijay Mishra, Ex. M.L.A.

He further submits that although during investigation when the statements of the informant and his family members were recorded then they tried to implicate the applicant by stating that applicant also took possession over the property of the informant along with co-accused Vijay Mishra, his father and also by illegal means transferred the amount from the firm of the informant but from the perusal of the statements of the witnesses recorded during investigation, it appears that only vague and general allegations have been made against the applicant and principal accused appears to be co-accused Vijay Mishra, the father of applicant.

15. Learned counsel for the applicant submits that although during investigation in Parcha no.8 of the case diary, Investigating Officer noted that amount of Rs. 3,82,000/- were transferred in the Vishnu Mishra vs State Of U.P. on 20 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/139477586/
3 account of applicant from the firm of the informant but as already mentioned there was business relationship between informant and the firm of the family of the applicant, therefore, amount was transferred from the account of the firm to the account of the applicant and admittedly applicant did not withdraw any amount directly from the bank and there is no evidence on record, which can suggests that applicant by playing fraud got transferred the above noted amount in his account.

16. He further submits that during investigation statement of Branch Manager of HDFC bank of Gopiganj Branch was recorded and he stated that in the current bank account of the informant two mobile numbers were provided and one mobile number was of applicant but during investigation Investigating Officer intentionally did not disclose the details of second mobile number which in fact belongs to the son of the informant.
17.

He further submits that during investigation it also revealed that Email ID of applicant is linked with the account of the firm but as when the above noted current account was opened then at that time relationship of the applicant and informant was cordial one, therefore, on the request of informant applicant provided his Email ID, therefore, merely on the basis of Email ID of the applicant, it cannot be said that applicant involved in commission of any fraud and cheating and further, actually above noted bank account does not individually belongs to the informant but it belongs to firm M/s Krishna Mohan Tiwari a partnership firm, in which, mother of the applicant is also one of the partner along with Ashok Shukla
and as name of the firm and the name of the informant is same, therefore, informant is trying to misuse the same.

18. Learned counsel for the applicant further submits that although applicant in the present matter could not earlier appear before the court concerned and he was arrested on 24.07.2022 but he did not abscond intentionally.
As FIR of the present case was politically motivated therefore, applicant was having serious threat of his life, therefore, he earlier could not appear only to save his life.
He further submits, while he was evading his arrest eight false cases have been lodged against him.

He further submits that with the help of local police informant lodged 15 FIRs against applicant and his entire family members including his parents, married sisters and their respective husbands and other relatives and details of the entire cases have been given in paragraph 31 to the affidavit filed in support of present application.
19. He further submits that informant is also having criminal history of 10 cases and his entire criminal history has been disclosed in paragraph 32 to the affidavit.

20. He further submits that applicant has been made accused in the present matter only due to the reason that he is son of Ex. M.L.A. co-accused Vijay Mishra and no specific and direct allegation has been made against him and it appears from the perusal of the FIR that entire allegation is against his father co-accused Vijay Mishra, Ex. M.L.A. and he is the principal accused in the present matter.
He further submits, applicant in the present matter is in jail since 24.07.2022 i.e. for last about nine months and till date trial of the case could not be concluded.

sentences.text: Per contra, learned AGA as well as learned counsel appearing on behalf of the informant vehemently opposed the prayer for bail and submitted that applicant is the son of co-accused Vijay Mishra, the Ex. M.L.A. and there is specific allegation against the applicant and his parents that they forcibly possessed the property of the informant and thereafter by playing fraud took over the possession of his firm and are continuously withdrawing and transferring the amount from his firm.

22. They further submits that during investigation Investigating Officer also collected evidence against the applicant, which shows that the mobile number of the applicant was linked with the current bank account of the firm M/s Krishna Mohan Tiwari, which in fact is not a partnership firm but it is a firm of informant.

Both the counsels further submits that on the basis of forged documents his family members claimed that the firm M/s Krishna Mohan Tiwari is a partnership firm and on the basis of forged document they also opened bank account and from the perusal of the details of the Pan card etc. of the informant, it appears that informant is the sole proprietor of the firm.
23.

Learned counsel for the informant and learned AGA further submits that applicant is an absconder and FIR of the present case was lodged on 04.08.2020 but he could only be arrested on 14.07.2022 i.e. after about two years and this fact clearly suggests that he tried to evade his arrest for almost two years.

24. Both the counsels further submits that applicant is also having a long criminal history of more than eight cases and this fact shows that applicant and his family members are hardened criminals and they are continuously misusing their political status.

25. Learned counsel for the informant and learned AGA further submits that father of the applicant was Ex. M.L.A. and is also having long criminal antecedents of more than 80 cases and in two of them he has been convicted.

26. They further urged, therefore, considering the nature of allegation, severity of punishment and criminal antecedents and political status of the family of the applicant, he should not be released on bail.
Conclusion 27.
I have heard learned counsels for both the parties at length and perused the record of the case.
28. Applicant is the son of Ex. M.L.A., Vijay Mishra and he belongs to a political party of U.P.

It appears from the FIR that although in the FIR there are several allegations but it appears that all the allegations are against co-accused Vijay Mishra, the father of the applicant, the Ex. M.L.A.
29.

In the FIR it is only stated against the applicant that Vijay Mishra, the co-accused i.e. father of the applicant after obtaining forged signature of the informant on cheques transferred the amount of the firm of the informant in his account and in the accounts of his wife and applicant and further,

30. Although, when the statement of the informant and other witnesses were recorded during investigation then they stated that applicant also involved along with his father in possessing the property of the informant and co-accused Vijay Mishra and his entire family including applicant are harassing the informant and his family since the year 2001 and along with Vijay Mishra, applicant also by playing fraud misappropriated the huge amount of the firm of the informant but even from the perusal of the statements of the witnesses recorded during investigation including statement of the informant, it appears that only general allegations have been made against the applicant and no specific allegation has been made against him and even from the perusal of the statements it appears that principal accused in the present matter is the father of the applicant i.e. co-accused Vijay Mishra.
31.

Further, as per FIR and the statements of witnesses including the statement of the informant,
informant and his family members are being harassed by co-accused Vijay Mishra, the father of the applicant and his family members including applicant since the year 2001 but FIR of the present case was lodged in August, 2020 i.e. after about two decades
, therefore, it appears that FIR of the present case was lodged by inordinate delay of about 20 years.

32. Although, during investigation when Investigating Officer perused the bank details of the alleged firm M/s Krishna Mohan Tiwari and recorded the statement of Branch Manager of HDFC Bank Gopiganj Branch then he found that mobile phone of the applicant was linked with the account of M/s Krishna Mohan Tiwari and from the account Rs. 3,82,000/- were also transferred in the account of applicant and in the bank, the Email ID of the applicant is also linked with the account of firm but in the FIR entire allegation is against the father of the applicant i.e. co-accused Vijay Mishra that he after taking possession over the firm of the informant misused the account of the firm and is continuously transferring the amount of the firm in the account of his son i.e. applicant and no allegation was made against applicant, therefore, from the FIR it reflects that allegation of cheating and fraud is against co-accused Vijay Mishra, the father of applicant.

33. Further, it is also pertinent to note here that a dispute is pending between informant and applicant side with regard to firm M/s Krishna Mohan Tiwari and with regard to dispute of the firm case is also pending before this Court.
Further, there is an arbitration clause in the partnership deed and pursuant thereof this Court has also appointed an Arbitrator.

34. Further, from the perusal of the record, it reflects that a dispute between the informant and family of the applicant is pending with regard to the cheques which were issued by the informant and were dishonoured and
in this regard criminal proceedings under Section 138 N.I. Act are also pending against the informant.

35. Therefore, from the discussion made above, it appears that disputes with regard to the partnership of the firm and with regard to cheques are pending between the family of applicant and Vishnu Mishra vs State Of U.P. on 20 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/139477586/

sentences.text: 36. However, it appears that applicant absconded for about two years but in the present matter he is in jail since July, 2022 i.e. for last about nine months.

Further, although criminal antecedents of an accused is having its own importance while deciding the bail applications and applicant is also having criminal history of more than eight cases but criminal history of the applicant has been explained in paragraphs-31 and 34 to the affidavit filed in support of present bail application.
In paragraph no. 34, eight cases have been explained and all the pending cases appears to be lodged after the lodgement of the FIR of the present case.
Further, from the perusal of the paragraph 32 to the affidavit, it appears that informant is also having criminal history of ten cases.

37. Further, as there is no specific allegation against the applicant in the present matter and it appears that co-accused Vijay Mishra, Ex. M.L.A. is the principal accused, therefore, it would not be appropriate to refuse bail to the applicant on the basis of his criminal history.
Criminal history of an accused although has importance but if otherwise case of bail is made out then merely on the basis of criminal history bail application of an accused should not be dismissed.
The law is settled that bail application neither can be rejected for punitive purposes nor for preventive purposes.

38. As in the present matter prima facie it appears that principal accused is the father of the applicant i.e. co-accused Vijay Mishra, Ex. M.L.A. and with regard to the firm M/s Krishna Mohan Tiwari a dispute between both the parties is pending even before this Court and applicant in the present matter is in jail since 24.07.2022 i.e. for last about nine months, therefore, in my considered view, applicant is entitled to be released on bail.
39. Accordingly, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the instant bail application is allowed.

40. Let the applicant - Vishnu Mishra be released on bail in the aforesaid case on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions:-
(i) The applicant shall appear before the trial court on the dates fixed, unless his personal presence is exempted.

(ii) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly, make inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
(iii) The applicant shall not indulge in any criminal and anti-social activity.
41. In case of breach of any of the above condition, the prosecution will be at liberty to move an application before this Court for cancellation of the bail of the applicant.
